steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Look at you, even now irresolute, an ocean fish lost in its course.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (She glances at him.)

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: You wish to know where I have brought you. You very much mind. You have not the qualification to take part in our congregation, yet your eyes tell me, you wish to know just what we will do to her.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Did you recover the kindred love between you? Could your heart be torn apart by what happened to your old relation? Do you feel it is unjust? Are you thus angered?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You are attempting to find what you cannot see.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: But of course. That is the expected response.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: You believe I wish to harm her. You are wrong. I wish to help her.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Only by elucidating where her—where all your pain lies at its source, can I better assist you in excising the problem point, is that not so?

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: As with you. You voluntarily became one of us, wishing to melt into the ocean true. Once you have completed this mission, your sordid nature will achieve purification. This is the ocean's charity to you.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: And in the end, charity alike will be extended to all your old relations. So long as they alike can relinquish their narrow views of a past enmity.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: To reunite you, that is the first step. To fathom you, that is the second step. And come the end, you will fathom us too.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: If you are able to reduce the nonsense by a measure, we may cooperate so much more harmoniously.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: I can also speak of things that will make you happy. Your old relation—the lucid one, she is already here.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Skadi?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: She is not here.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Naturally, she is not. Without my invitation, none may enter this place.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: She's entered the city. You know that.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: You have expressed surprise. That is very interesting. There is no sound in this city that I do not hear.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: And He admires all I do, has granted me the power, given my life further reach. My perception, my wit, all are no longer bound by the flesh you see before you.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: I am approaching perfection. I will accept your grudges.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: As for your old relation, now—her arrival was sooner than anticipated.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: 'Abyssal Hunters are bound by blood.'

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: She has no inkling of what awaits her. All you had to do was take the other away, and she has given chase here, not having once rested.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Truly a camaraderie to make one gasp. Does she know the state of you nowadays? What will she do when she confronts a traitor? Will she trust in your blood binding, old comrades rekindled, or will a blade pierce true through your body?

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: I have great expectations.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (She turns to leave.)

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: You needn't hurry to find her. You've done very well. You have brought this one back to where she should remain, and led another into the city.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: He will be very pleased.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: He?

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: You need not know.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: We simply wait now. We wait until the time comes, and naturally, you may find your old relation then, and pass on to her our invitation.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: She is not sure to come.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: She will come. She will come seeking me herself.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You're back again!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: We live in the best building in the whole north area. Look, this door still closes. A door that shuts closed is one of your best friends on a rainy day.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: People are nearby. Two of them.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: They're, well, they're usually here.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant
steps.text: One-hundred-and-thirty, one-hundred-and-thirty-one, one-hundred-and-thirty-two...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Hi, Brick, are you doing good today?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant
steps.text: One, two, three...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I'm sorry!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Poor guy, now he has to start over again. He's always sitting here, counting all the bricks in the street. Don't tell him I said, but each day's count isn't much like the last.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: And also, that one's Stonecolumn. He likes making his way all around the street pillars. When it's all dark and rainy he doesn't come out. He's a little old, and his legs start hurting when he gets wet.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You can just ignore them, and they'll ignore you too, just like they ignore me.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Come in, singer. Let me give you an official introduction. In here is my home.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Hi, Sheetmetal. Hi, Drywall. You're awake!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Strokes case)

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Ouch...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Hey, Woodframe. You brought this outside person into the house again.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She's not bad.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: She's from the outside.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Bench has taken a decent liking to her, haven't you, Bench?

steps.name: Young Inhabitant
steps.text: Wgh... aogh...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Don't—Don't bite! You're going to chew the singer's skirt apart!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: *cough*.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Not that it'll come apart.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It's all slobbery again. That's not very pretty.

steps.name: Young Inhabitant
steps.text: Aogh, au-auwgh...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: This rascal really has taken a shining to you, singer.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You see? Bench wants her to stay too.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You are scheming something. Do not think, I do not know.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: This will not, end well.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I'm not, okay, I don't have any plans at all.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: What is the phrase...? Suit yourself.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: The rules, may not be broken.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Whether by you, or by her.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: I will be watching.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: We shall go.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Phew... they finally left.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, don't be afraid. This is just the kind of person Sheetmetal is. He may seem very frightful, but he won't really do anything to us.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Okay, I know you're not afraid. Since you're so much more powerful than them.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I just wanted to say, if he really tried something—*snort*—I wouldn't be scared of him either.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You're sighing.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: This barrel's empty. So is the tray.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Let me just think... maybe there's still some food under the bed.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Is this the bed?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It is. Does it seem very odd? Were the beds in your home not metal?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't mind too much.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You can find wooden beds in some houses, too. Wood's surprisingly useful. Wood can burn, and make houses brighter and warmer at once. There are some times if you fall ill here when the winters won't be kind to you.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Eh-heh—look, this is my treasure box. I filled it a touch full when I woke up this morning.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Help me for a moment here, get this dry seagrass out of my sight. No, don't throw it on the floor. Even if we can't eat it, we can still pad out the bed with it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You have a lot.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: That's right. I hide everything useful inside here.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Take a look at this, they're clothes I'm sewing right now. I sharpened up a shell into a needle recently, and it's so much better to use than all those years-old ones.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I'm fairly short of material. Still need to go searching properly through the city south. Maybe there'll be some buried so deep that nobody's taken it yet.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It'll be getting cold soon, so I need to hurry up.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: No, don't you dare, Bench, you can't touch these clothes! These are for Grandma Petra. Her cough just keeps getting worse.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Not this either! You let go!

steps.name: Young Inhabitant
steps.text: Woodframe.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I've told you how many times? It's not Woodframe, it's Pictureframe!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Also, you can't even eat this! There's no point in you even having it!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Woodframe... Pictureframe?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You heard them calling me that?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I only know you as Anita.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I picked Anita for myself... I heard it in one of Grandma Petra's stories. She was a girl just like you, she could really sing. It sounds much nicer than Woodframe, doesn't it?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Most of us here have no names. Whatever came to mind first is what we use. Brick's always counting bricks, Sheetmetal has a sheetmetal fence running all around his house.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: They call me Woodframe. Because underneath this pictureframe is where Grandma Petra found me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You mentioned your own mother before.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She didn't give me up to anyone else. Brave, she was. When I was born, there were no children here. Children couldn't survive.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Those years, nobody dared go against Grandma Petra... she gave me a share of food. Don't let her poor health now fool you, she's this city's most fearsome person by far.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Even Sheetmetal fears her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Things are much better now. That priest taught us how to survive. Just look at Bench, and those children over there. I believe in this place of ours becoming a lively one someday.

steps.name: Young Inhabitant
steps.text: Aaah... ah...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: So long as you don't keep taking what's mine. You're a good kid still, aren't you, Bench?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It doesn't matter if anything else gets taken away. Every night when I go to sleep, I hide this box away. They wouldn't know how to find it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Ugh, we don't really go 'yours' or 'mine' here. I understand hiding things is bad. Singer, you won't go telling anyone else, will you? You're not interested in my things to boot.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Do you trust in me?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You're a guest. Grandma Petra taught me that we should properly receive guests.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: There it is, I knew it was there. Look, there's still one fin left.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This odor...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It's half a month old. Still quite fresh as fish go.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Pull it apart, and this half... is for Bench. Here, Bench, food for you here!

steps.name: Young Inhabitant
steps.text: Ah... aaah... (He swallows it.)

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Alright, and this half is for you. Leave the bones when you're done eating. I can boil some soup with them after.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I can go to find food too.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: But the day still hasn't come! If you went out now, you probably couldn't find anything to eat.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Can't say until you try.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She talks, and suddenly she's gone. Seriously, how odd she is!

a.text: The wandering singer in the red dress, carrying her tremendous case on her back, strolls casually through the street.
Still no one heeds her. In a street still and ashen, naught moves but a flutter of red.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Still following.

a.text: Skadi suddenly picks up in speed.
The indistinct shadow sweeps through the way, in the manner of a wave driven on by a gale.
It is as if she is about to charge headlong into the ocean—and then comes to a sudden halt.

The singer in the red dress clutches her harp to her chest, using one hand to clamber a nomadic city's wreckage, her vision sweeping past the chapel towering on the high cliff, resting on the pitch-black sea surface.
From a crag hanging over ten meters high, she leaps down.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: The shore. She has gone to the shore.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Yes, Sheetmetal, your thinking is correct. She wants to enter the sea. She intends to set into it.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: The time, is not yet come.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: The priest spoke so. The tide must flood and ebb one-hundred times, before we are permitted, to enter the sea.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal, we cannot come here. The shore, does not permit us to.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: That is meaningless. We will, block her.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Block her? As if we could defeat her?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: The priest spoke, we must wait one hundred times, before we may go. It is only, the ninety-ninth time now.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: She will obtain nothing at all. The shore today, has nothing at all.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: So what is she looking for?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal, it is bitterly cold here, I am hungry, we cannot come here, and you should not ask.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Is there anything in the sea?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: I do not know.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Even if you knew, what then?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: I do not know. Sheetmetal, what you say, I do not know any of. I do not understand.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Where is the furthest we have traveled, in the past?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: The westernmost of the west. A long time ago. In those days, we were, no taller than this. We could still, collect food in the town.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Borderline. We do not often, say this word. We have seen, this city's, edge.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: That was you, Sheetmetal, not we.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: At that time, I was dizzy with hunger.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: You said, you wanted to go further still. You wanted, to push your luck.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: It was to try my luck.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Hmph. You never could, make any sense. The priest gave you such years of teaching. You never could learn.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Heh-heh, Sheetmetal, you make. Sense of me.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You said so, at that time too.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You have always trusted me. You let me take the can you kept. I traveled another day.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: And then you came back.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Yes, I came back.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: You ate nothing, for several days after. I thought, you wanted to starve yourself to death.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: I thought of it. But what meaning, would starving myself have?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: After all, we will all perish come not too long.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: You are giving me a shock. You said this back then too. I do not know what you are talking about.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Afterward... the priest came. It was only when he came, that I felt a change. We all changed.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: The priest, has a good life. He says we can have one. What he says is true.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: It is true. Because... it is the truth. He let us see it.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Because of the priest, I survived. We all survived. That is, very good.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: That line, no one can cross.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Is that line, the seawater line?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: All lines. Just like the traps Woodframe makes. They stop, even outsiders.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: We cannot exit either. That is for the best.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal... your leg, is going to meet the water!

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Water... yes. I shall not cross.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Even if I crossed over... crossed over, there may well be nothing there at all.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Phew... Sheetmetal, you finally stopped walking. You scared me just now.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Do not be like that, asking so many questions. You are like Woodframe, when you always ask. She was always strange. The priest said too that something is wrong about her, did he not?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Questioning... cannot help us.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Only answers have any meaning.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: You impress me so, Sheetmetal. You are the only one who remembers, the priest's words as strongly.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Look, she has not stopped walking along the shore.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal, where are you going? Are you going to follow too? No, that is not right, we may not, and cannot follow her!

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Even I know, we cannot defeat her. We have no way to drive her out.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: She cannot return now.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: That... That is a very good thing for us.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: I want the big case she has. There is surely much to eat inside.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: The case is not here. She took it.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: There is only this... this, she placed it on the rocks. I do not know what this is.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: She is always holding it. It should be something good, no?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: May I... May I try a bite, Sheetmetal? I am so very hungry.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: (Plink-plunk)

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: What—What is this? I have never heard a sound like this before.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: (Plink-plunk, plink-plunk)

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Stop it quickly, Sheetmetal, this sound is making my stomach and teeth shake without end. If you are fond of holding it then hold it. I am going back after all.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: No meaning. This also has no meaning.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: This useless thing. It should be left on the ground. To rot.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The whole way, I thought it was somebody else following me.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: You—You returned! How were you able? Nobody who goes to, the shore at this time, will return.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You want to enter the sea.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm just taking a walk around the area.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Is there anything in the sea?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: There's nothing at all.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: That cannot be.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: You have turned stranger and stranger, Sheetmetal. You are still asking these questions I do not understand. Did we not come here to block her?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Now she is heading back. We may go back.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You saw it. You know.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal, you are shaking. Have you become ill?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't come near.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: And what if I do? Will you beat us so we are lying on the floor, like before?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: There is something in the sea, correct?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't move.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Aaaaagh—

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Drywall!

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: This stone... her movements, are truly fast.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Was that a sound from my mouth? Sheetmetal, I made a sound. My heart is beating wild. Have I become ill too?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: I believe, your head will explode with a bang. Just like a shell smashed open, there will be something shining bright white inside.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Will I die then?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: We will know the next time we try. What has fallen apart now is something else. I have never seen a thing like this before.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Why can it... still move?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Run. Head back to the city. Quickly.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: —Remember to leave my harp here.
